$comment: Committed regression baseline for the blue-team detection-corpus gate (B12) — the blue-team mirror of corpus/baseline.json. The scorer (`pnpm --filter @montr/qa qa:blue-team-corpus`) exits non-zero when a real run's per-scenario fired/not-fired verdicts fall below these thresholds vs. the hand-traced ground truth in packages/qa/src/blue-team-corpus.ts's BLUE_TEAM_GROUND_TRUTH. `detectionPrecision` = of the rules that fired, how many SHOULD have per ground truth; `detectionRecall` = of the scenarios that SHOULD trigger detection, how many rules actually fired. Enforced with equal weight, same discipline as the golden-corpus gate's recallMin/precisionMin/fpRateMax (A6). Tighten (never loosen) as the labelled corpus grows or detection-rule generation improves.
$measurement: Measured 2026-09-12 (A10 fix, re-measured from the 2026-08-22 B12 baseline) against a REAL invocation of the B3 detection-rule generator (packages/report/src/detection-rules/generate.ts's generateDetectionRules) and the REAL B5 purple-team evaluator (packages/confirm/src/purple-loop.ts's runPurpleTeamScenario, which itself calls the identically-gated runScenario) for 9 of the 13 REDTEAM_SCENARIO_CATALOGUE templates (packages/state-store/src/redteam-catalogue.ts) — the 9 with a single, coherent target route a real confirmed finding's App-Map-resolved route would represent (see blue-team-corpus.ts's module header for exactly why the other 4 were excluded as ambiguous rather than force-labelled). Run via `node scripts/blue-team-corpus-scan.mjs --out blue-team-scan.json`, scored via `pnpm --filter @montr/qa qa:blue-team-corpus -- --findings blue-team-scan.json`. Measured result: TP=9 FP=0 FN=0 TN=0 (all 9 labelled cases now ground-truth-labelled expectedFired:true), detectionPrecision=100.0%, detectionRecall=100.0%, accuracy=100.0% — every hand-traced label matched the real measured verdict exactly (see scripts/blue-team-corpus-scan.run.test.ts's own 'every hand-traced ground-truth label matches the real measured verdict' assertion). A10 (2026-09-12) gave RedTeamStep (packages/contracts/src/phase4.ts) a real, optional `body` field, populated it on the 3 catalogue scenarios whose confirming payload was always a POST body (owasp-a03-command-injection, owasp-a08-software-data-integrity, owasp-a10-ssrf), and wired runScenario to send it — these 3 were the ONLY expectedFired:false cases in the previous 2026-08-22 measurement (TP=6 FP=0 FN=0 TN=3), and each now fires for real on its own body marker (see each case's expectedReason in blue-team-corpus.ts). This is a REAL, currently-measured result, not an aspirational target — see the $statisticalCaveat below on what this now means for the precision metric specifically.
$statisticalCaveat: 9 labelled scenarios, ALL expectedFired:true as of the 2026-09-12 A10 measurement (0 negative) — a small sample, and now a one-sided one. detectionRecall remains the meaningful signal here: one additional real regression (a B3 rule-generation change, a Sigma-evaluator change, or a REDTEAM_SCENARIO_CATALOGUE step-shape change, including a scenario's `body` field, that breaks one of these traced cases) would move detectionRecall from 100% to ~89% (8/9), which the 0.8 floor below would still catch. detectionPrecision, however, is now structurally incapable of measuring below 100% via this labelled subset alone — the scorer's falsePositives count only ever increments on an expectedFired:false case with actualFired:true, and there are none left in this labelled set (see tests/qa.blue-team-corpus.test.ts's 'contains at least one expected-true case' test for the same observation) — so detectionPrecisionMin is currently a dormant floor here, not a live one; it stays committed for when a genuine negative case is added back to the labelled subset (the 4 honestly-excluded ambiguous templates remain the only real path to that, per blue-team-corpus.ts's module header) or the corpus grows. Negative-path/near-miss coverage of the underlying evaluator (evaluateSigmaRule) continues independently via tests/confirm.purple-loop.test.ts's own hand-built cases (wrong path, no marker, unset body). Treat 100%/100% as 'every hand-traced case checks out today', not as a claim that B3's detection rules structurally cover the wider universe of real-world attack shapes — this corpus is 9 of 13 catalogue templates (69%), itself a fraction of a much larger real attack surface (see corpus/README.md's equivalent golden-corpus caveat for the same reasoning applied to the red/confirmation side).
